messages:
maria: Ran the cross-GPU sweep for max_tokens_per_batch and token-budget heuristics this morning. Quick summary: A10/T4/L4/A100/H100, measured p99 latency, tokens/sec, and KV cache miss rate. Posting raw numbers and notes below.

chris: Nice — are these end-to-end requests (including IO) or pure kernel time?

maria: end-to-end from HTTP ingress -> egress on our staging infra. Logs filtered for identical prompt dist (mostly short+some long).

maria: Raw CSV (gpu, max_tokens_per_batch, p99_ms, tokens_per_sec, kv_miss_pct):
```
A10,16000,135,7900,3.2
T4,8000,210,4200,5.1
L4,10000,165,6100,4.0
A100,32000,95,15200,2.0
H100,24000,120,13700,9.8
```

devon: H100 kv_miss_pct looks bad — 9.8% is new. Did we flip the KV cache eviction policy?

maria: No config flip. I profiled traces and saw frequent cache invalidations during large-batch merges on H100. Stacktrace snippet:
```
[merge_batch] -> allocate_kv_backing() -> evict_pages_if_needed() -> page_table_flush

hot path spends ~18% on page_table ops for H100 at 24k tokens/batch
```

tao: Kernel selection log: noticed we fell back from fast-fused-attn to cu_attn_fallback when seq>2048 for H100 in that run. Likely because our heuristic uses sequence-length-only threshold; long cumulative token batches push the allocator to a different layout.

chris: So two problems: (1) large max_tokens_per_batch triggers fallback kernels on H100, (2) KV backing allocs thrash and raise miss rate. Both hit latency and throughput.

sara: For the continuous batcher maybe prefer token-budget packing that caps per-request seq len impact. Suggest queue policy: prefer filling with many short seqs instead of few long seqs when budget near limit. That reduces seq variance and keeps kernel selection in fast path.

maria: Did a quick sim with altered queue policy: favor_short_first = true. Re-ran A100/H100 at same max_tokens targets, results: H100 p99 down to 108ms, kv_miss_pct -> 4.6%, tokens_per_sec ~14100. A100 unchanged (still good).

devon: Any regressions for T4/L4/A10 after that change? T4 improved slightly (p99 205->198) due to more compact packing, no regressions observed.

tao: Also changed kernel-selection gating: instead of single seq threshold 2048, use estimated per-batch-peak-seq = max(seq_i) and aggregate_tokens heuristic — prefer fused-attn if peak_seq * batch_size <= kernel_limit. That prevented fallback for many H100 cases.

maria: With that kernel gating + prefer_short_first we can bump H100 max_tokens_per_batch back up somewhat. New recommended per-GPU targets (for continuous-batching token budget):
- A10: 16000 tokens/batch
- T4: 8000 tokens/batch
- L4: 12000 tokens/batch (bumped; L4 handles mid-range well)
- A100: 32000 tokens/batch
- H100: 27000 tokens/batch (with new kernel gating and prefer_short_first queue policy)

chris: +1 to those numbers. We should gate rollout behind a short canary: pick 10% of traffic on dedicated pool, run for 24h, monitor p99 and kv_miss_pct. If kv_miss_pct > 6% trigger rollback.

sara: I'll add a queue-policy flag `prefer_short_first` to runtime conf and expose an override per-deployment. Also add metrics: batch_peak_seq, batch_token_budget, kv_evictions/sec.

ci-bot: deploy-plan created: pr#4587 -> canary 10% eng-runtime/dedicated/h100 -> health checks: p99, kv_miss_pct, tokens_per_sec -> rollback trigger kv_miss_pct>6% OR p99>1.2x baseline.

maria: I'll open the PR with the kernel gating change and include microbench harness logs. Attaching a quick perf diff snippet:
```
H100 @24k old: p99 120ms tokens/sec 13700 kv_miss 9.8%
H100 @24k new: p99 104ms tokens/sec 13950 kv_miss 4.6%
```

devon: Nice win. After canary we should also run a long-tail eval with adversarial long-seqs to validate no hidden regressions.

maria: Agreed. I'll add an eval set and schedule overnight run. Thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
